answer_text:
For the hyperbola

\[
x^2-y^2=1,
\]

we have \(a=b=1\), so

\[
c=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}=\sqrt2,\qquad e=\frac ca=\sqrt2.
\]

Thus the right focus and right directrix are

\[
F=(\sqrt2,0),\qquad l:x=\frac1{\sqrt2}.
\]

For any point \(P=(x,y)\) on the right branch, \(x\ge 1\). Its distance to \(F\) is

\[
|PF|^2=(x-\sqrt2)^2+y^2
= x^2-2\sqrt2x+2+x^2-1
=2x^2-2\sqrt2x+1
=(\sqrt2x-1)^2.
\]

Hence

\[
|PF|=\sqrt2x-1.
\]

Its distance to the directrix \(l\) is

\[
\operatorname{dist}(P,l)=x-\frac1{\sqrt2}.
\]

Therefore

\[
\operatorname{dist}(P,l)=\frac{|PF|}{\sqrt2}.
\]

Let

\[
p=|AF|,\qquad q=|BF|.
\]

Since \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AB\), and \(l\) is vertical,

\[
|MN|=\operatorname{dist}(M,l)
=\frac{\operatorname{dist}(A,l)+\operatorname{dist}(B,l)}2
=\frac{p+q}{2\sqrt2}.
\]

Also, because \(AF\perp BF\), triangle \(AFB\) is right-angled at \(F\), so

\[
|AB|^2=p^2+q^2,
\]

and therefore

\[
|AB|=\sqrt{p^2+q^2}.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{|MN|}{|AB|}
=
\frac{p+q}{2\sqrt2\sqrt{p^2+q^2}}.
\]

By Cauchy’s inequality,

\[
(p+q)^2\le 2(p^2+q^2),
\]

so

\[
p+q\le \sqrt{2(p^2+q^2)}.
\]

Hence

\[
\frac{|MN|}{|AB|}
\le
\frac{\sqrt{2(p^2+q^2)}}{2\sqrt2\sqrt{p^2+q^2}}
=
\frac12.
\]

Equality occurs when \(p=q\). This is attainable, for example with

\[
A=\left(\frac{3\sqrt2}{4},\frac{\sqrt2}{4}\right),
\qquad
B=\left(\frac{3\sqrt2}{4},-\frac{\sqrt2}{4}\right),
\]

which lie on the hyperbola and satisfy \(AF\perp BF\).

Therefore the maximum value is

\[
\boxed{\frac12}
\]
